A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TQNet research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original TQNet forecasting results, ablations, efficiency measurements, and robustness experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains the original forecasting, ablation, efficiency, and robustness results, including the supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The periodically shifted temporal queries, attention mechanism, MLP, normalization, and prediction procedure are unchanged. Section 3 and Appendix A.1 retain the same equations and pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 datasets and retain the same multivariate and multivariate-to-univariate tasks. The PEMS horizon corrections do not introduce additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main comparisons, the iTransformer/PatchTST/DLinear integration study, the multivariate-to-univariate comparison, and the ETS comparison.

E3.justification: V2 revises the reported PEMS horizons from {96,192,336,720} in Table 5 and several captions to {12,24,48,96}, explicitly distinguishing PEMS from other datasets in Section 4.1. V1 Tables 4 and 9 already use the shorter horizons, supporting a correction of the stated protocol rather than evidence of rerun experiments. Other settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The query/key and component ablations, integration study, representation visualization, covariate analysis, periodicity sensitivity, stacking, look-back sensitivity, and robustness studies retain the same questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 retains the default seed of 2024. Table 9 retains seeds 2024–2026, learning-rate comparisons, and the same mean and standard-deviation reporting; no statistical procedures are added.

E6.justification: The reported error scores, rankings, and plotted outcomes are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The PEMS edits correct the horizons attached to existing scores; they do not supply new scores or demonstrate a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Section 3 and Appendix A remain unchanged, including the correlation-alignment and periodic-averaging reasoning in Appendix A.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about robust correlation modeling, forecasting accuracy across 12 datasets, and efficiency comparable to linear methods.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including dependence on periodicity, weak inter-variable correlations, diminishing benefits with longer look-back windows, and challenges with multiple periodicities.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, hardware, optimizer, training budget, hyperparameters, and stated code-access information are unchanged. The horizon edits reconcile previously reported settings rather than add implementation or resource-access details.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and research positioning are unchanged, including the connection to CycleNet and the distinction among channel-mixing, channel-independent, and channel-dependent approaches.

P1.justification: V2 adds a short dataset-specific horizon explanation in Section 4.1 and makes localized caption wording changes. Section ordering and nearly all existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 is repositioned, Figure 4 moves from page 7 to page 8, and surrounding content reflows. Several captions and Table 5 horizon labels are revised; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves misleading PEMS horizon labels and aligns the setup and captions with the shorter horizons already present in v1's ablation and seed tables. This improves the consistency and interpretability of the evaluation reporting, while leaving the method and empirical evidence unchanged.
